Validate a hydrolocation set before building from it

Source: R/check_hydrolocation_input.R
check_hydrolocation_input.Rd

Checks a hydrolocation GeoPackage against what the pipeline requires of it. Gated checks are properties a build depends on; informational ones report shape without judging it.

Gated: the layer is named so the pipeline can read it; geometry is POINT and non-empty; the CRS is defined; hl_reference and flowpath_id are populated; no row is an exact duplicate of another; every vpuid names a unit some supplied reference carries; and every flowpath_id resolves to a reach in its domain's reference.

Reported: how many rows share an hl_reference (collocation is by design, since several hydrolocations may collapse onto one POI), how many arrive with a poi_id, and the mix of hl_type.

Usage

check_hydrolocation_input(
  hl_gpkg,
  layer = "hydrolocations",
  references = list(),
  check_distance = TRUE,
  max_dist_m = 200,
  strict = FALSE
)

Arguments

hl_gpkg

Path to the hydrolocation GeoPackage.

layer

Layer to read. Default "hydrolocations", which is the name the pipeline reads; a set whose layer is called anything else is rejected unless this is set explicitly, because the build cannot find it.

references

Named list of references to resolve against, each a list of ids (character flowpath_id) and vpuids. Built by hl_reference_index() when not supplied directly.

check_distance

If TRUE (default), also measure how far each point lies from the reach it names. Resolution is not placement: an identifier can exist and still name a reach on the other side of the domain, which is what a statewide point set indexed against a clipped reference produces.

max_dist_m

Reporting threshold for that distance, in metres. Default 200. The result is informational, not a gate: across the NWM v4 inputs the population is nowhere zero, and a threshold tight enough to catch genuine mis-attribution also flags several thousand forecast points that sit a few hundred metres off the reference line and snap cleanly. Read the spread the check reports, a median near zero with a long tail is snapping noise, a median in the kilometres is a point set indexed against the wrong domain.

strict

If TRUE, a failed gate raises an error. Default FALSE reports every check and returns.

Value

Invisibly, a list with ok, stage and one entry per check.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
refs <- list(conus = hl_reference_index("conus_reference.gpkg"))
check_hydrolocation_input("merged_hydrolocations.gpkg", references = refs)
} # }
